comparisons.peer_topic: Inventory write-down impact on gross margin
comparisons.peer_summary: If assumptions regarding future demand or market conditions become less favorable, additional inventory write-downs may be required, negatively impacting gross margin; conversely, selling previously written-down inventory above its written-down value may result in a net benefit to gross margin.
comparisons.comparison: Both NVDA and AMD discuss the specific mechanics of how inventory provisions and releases impact gross margin. NVDA reports a specific net unfavorable impact of 2.7% in 2024 resulting from $2.2 billion in provisions offset by $540 million in releases. AMD discloses the policy that additional write-downs would negatively impact gross margin, while selling previously written-down inventory below its realized price results in a net benefit, which conceptually mirrors NVDA's reported provision release benefit, though AMD does not quantify these specific 2024 margin impacts in this text.

sentences.text: Provisions for inventory and excess inventory purchase obligations totaled $2.2 billion for both fiscal years 2024 and 2023.

Sales of previously reserved inventory or settlements of excess inventory purchase obligations resulted in a provision release of $540 million and $137 million for fiscal years 2024 and 2023, respectively.
The net effect on our gross margin was an unfavorable impact of 2.7% and 7.5% in fiscal years 2024 and 2023, respectively.

If in any period we anticipate a change in assumptions such as future demand or market conditions to be less favorable than our previous estimates, additional inventory write-downs may be required and would be reflected in cost of sales, resulting in a negative impact to our gross margin in that period.

If in any period we are able to sell inventories that had been written down to a level below the ultimate realized selling price in a previous period, related revenue would be recorded with a lower or no offsetting charge to cost of sales resulting in a net benefit to our gross margin in that period.

peer_results.rationale: The retrieved candidates (avgo_2024_7_D049, avgo_2024_7_D073) discuss gross margin drivers related to VMware amortization and employee withholding taxes, respectively. They do not contain specific disclosures regarding inventory provisions, write-downs, or the impact of inventory sell-through on gross margin, which is the specific topic of the NVDA disclosure.

comparisons.peer_summary: The 2024 unfavorable gross margin impacts were partially offset by favorable movements including lower period charges from sell-through of previously reserved inventory, lower non-accelerator reserves, lower excess capacity charges, and benefits from CHIPS Act government incentives.
comparisons.comparison: Both NVDA and INTC explicitly cite the sell-through of previously reserved inventory as a key driver for favorable gross margin movements (provision releases) in fiscal 2024. NVDA quantifies this as a $540 million provision release contributing to a net unfavorable margin impact of only 2.7% against $2.2 billion in provisions. INTC similarly identifies 'lower period charges driven by the sell-through of previously reserved inventory' as a primary offset to unfavorable gross margin impacts, confirming a shared industry dynamic of recovering value from prior reserves.

sentences.text: Sales of previously reserved inventory or settlements of excess inventory purchase obligations resulted in a provision release of $540 million and $137 million for fiscal years 2024 and 2023, respectively.

These 2024 unfavorable gross margin impacts were partially offset by certain favorable gross margin movements in 2024, including lower period charges driven by the sell-through of previously reserved inventory and lower non-accelerator reserves taken, lower period charges related to excess capacity charges, and a benefit recognized for government incentives received under the CHIPS Act.

comparisons.peer_summary: Consolidated gross margin improved to 22% in 2024 from -9% in 2023, aided by increased average selling prices and manufacturing cost reductions, despite the prior year's inventory write-downs and lower costs from selling previously written-down inventory in 2024.
comparisons.comparison: Both NVDA and MU disclose that the sale of previously written-down or reserved inventory provided cost benefits (provision releases) in fiscal 2024. NVDA reports a $540 million release. MU attributes its significant gross margin improvement (from -9% to 22%) partly to 'lower costs in 2024 from the sale of inventories written down in 2023.' Both disclosures highlight this mechanism as a contributing factor to the current year's margin performance, despite both also acknowledging prior year inventory write-downs.

sentences.text: Sales of previously reserved inventory or settlements of excess inventory purchase obligations resulted in a provision release of $540 million and $137 million for fiscal years 2024 and 2023, respectively.

Our consolidated gross margin percentage improved to 22% for 2024 from negative 9% for 2023, as a result of improvements in margins for both DRAM and NAND products, primarily due to increases in average selling prices, and manufacturing cost reductions, the effects of charges to write down inventories to their NRV in 2023 and lower costs in 2024 from the sale of inventories written down in 2023 (as detailed in "Inventory NRV write-downs" below).
